Adding one more concrete plugin use case here from the background-agent/delegation side.

We are building OpenCode plugin workflows where a primary agent can delegate work to background agents while continuing the main conversation. The missing UX surface is a low-noise, persistent footer/status item showing whether background agents are active, for example:

- `BG: idle`
- `BG: 2 running`
- `BG: sdd-verify +1`

Toasts are useful for completion events, but they are not a good fit for ongoing runtime state. Transcript/system-prompt injection is also the wrong layer because this is UI-only state and should not affect model context.

A hook like `tui.footer.items` would be enough for this use case: the plugin owns the runtime state, OpenCode owns placement/truncation/rendering. If #13885 lands with plugin-provided status line variables and a `session_footer` target, that could also solve this cleanly.

Thanks for pushing this — the direction looks right overall, especially keeping `bash` untouched for simple commands and routing PTY-heavy behavior through a separate tool.

A few review points I think are worth addressing before merge:

1. **Login shell args appear to be duplicated** in `packages/opencode/src/tool/terminal.ts`.
   Both `run` and `create` call `pty.create({ command: Shell.preferred(), args: Shell.login(Shell.preferred()) ? [-l] : [], ... })`, but `Pty.create()` already appends `-l` internally when `Shell.login(command)` is true (`packages/opencode/src/pty/index.ts`). That means login shells will likely get `-l -l`.

2. **`read` looks broken for cursor-based replay and final output capture**.
   In `terminal.ts`, `read` uses `pty.connect(session.ptyId, readWs, session.lastCursor)`, but `Pty.connect()` sends both replay data **and** the NUL-prefixed meta frame containing the real cursor. `createMockSocket()` currently decodes all frames into `newOutput`, so the meta frame gets mixed into output, and then `session.lastCursor += newOutput.length` advances by payload length rather than the actual PTY cursor.

   Related: once the PTY exits, `Pty` auto-removes the session in the core service. That means a persistent session can disappear from the PTY layer before `read` has a chance to fetch final output / exit state. I think this needs either:
   - explicit parsing of the meta cursor frame + storing cursor/output in `SessionState`, or
   - a different persistence model so `read` can still return the final buffered output after exit.

3. **The claimed backward compatibility for omitted `action` needs a real test**.
   The tool uses `z.discriminatedUnion(action, ...)` with `.default(run)` on the `RunAction` branch. I’m not confident that omission of the discriminator will actually parse as `run` with `discriminatedUnion`. The skipped tests make this especially important. I’d strongly suggest adding a test for calling the tool with no `action` field at all, because right now this may not actually be backward-compatible.

4. **There seems to be a duplicated focus effect** in `packages/app/src/pages/session/terminal-panel.tsx`.
   The `createEffect(on(() => [opened(), terminal.active()] ... focus(id)))` block appears twice.

5. **Agent-session detection by title prefix is probably too brittle**.
   The Desktop auto-open logic currently relies on `last.title.startsWith(Agent:)`. That works for now, but it feels easy to break if titles are customized/localized later. If there’s any way to tag agent-created PTYs structurally instead of inferring from the title, that would be more robust.

The two biggest concerns from my side are **(1) duplicated `-l`** and **(2) the `read` / cursor / exited-session behavior**, since those seem like real correctness issues rather than polish.

Happy to take another look after an update.

**Use case: umbrella coordination repo with 15+ nested git repos**

We use a coordination repo for cross-repo planning (OpenSpec artifacts, specs, tasks) with 15 independent product repos cloned into a gitignored `projects/` directory. Agent sessions routinely span the umbrella and 2-3 project repos in a single session.

**File search is already solved**, we work around the indexing limitation by adding `!projects/*` to a `.ignore` file ([docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/tools/#internals)), which makes ripgrep include project files for `@` search. This works well.

**The remaining gap is git diff visibility.** When the agent edits files inside `projects/acme-backend/`, OpenCode Desktop's diff panel shows nothing, because OpenCode resolves the git root by walking up from `cwd` to the nearest `.git`, and never scans for nested git repositories within the workspace. Each project has its own `.git` that OpenCode doesn't detect.

This means:
- No diff review for agent changes in nested repos
- No change tracking across multi-repo sessions
- No visibility into uncommitted work across projects

**Request**: When workspace folders land, they should also register additional git roots for the diff panel, not just file indexing and permission scoping. VS Code handles this via `git.autoRepositoryDetection`, which scans for nested `.git` directories and adds each as a separate Source Control provider.

For the workspace folders feature, git awareness would mean:
- Detecting `.git` in each workspace folder (or its children)
- Showing each as a separate diff provider in the Desktop diff panel
- Aggregated change indicators (e.g., "acme-backend: 3 changes, acme-notifications: 1 change")

This is currently the biggest workflow friction for multi-repo development in OpenCode Desktop. File search and permissions are solvable with `.ignore`, diff blindness is not.

I have this fix running in production on my fork. A few notes:

**[Console]::OutputEncoding alone is not enough.** Three encoding layers need to be set for PowerShell:

| Setting | Scope |
|---------|-------|
| `chcp 65001` | Console code page |
| `[Console]::OutputEncoding` | .NET output encoding |
| `$OutputEncoding` | PowerShell pipeline encoding |

**cmd.exe also needs the same fix.** The cmd() function has two branches:
1. PS.has(name) -> PowerShell: needs all three settings
2. Otherwise -> cmd.exe: needs `chcp 65001 > nul &&` prefix

Without the cmd.exe branch fix, commands that fall through to cmd.exe will still produce garbled output.

https://github.com/fkyah3/opencode-fkyah3/blob/pr/cjk-encoding-fix/packages/opencode/src/tool/bash.ts
